questions.question: The Ramoshi Uprising of 1824 took place in which of the following present states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ramoshi Uprising of 1824 took place in the present state of Maharashtra.
 
• The Ramoshi community, primarily residing in Maharashtra, revolted against the British East India Company.
 
• The uprising was led by Chittur Singh, a notable leader of the Ramoshi tribe.
 
• The Ramoshis were dissatisfied with British policies that impacted their traditional way of life and economic conditions.
 
• This uprising was one of the early revolts against British colonial rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramoshi Community**

 
 
• The Ramoshis are a tribal community found mainly in Maharashtra and parts of Karnataka.
 
• Traditionally, they were known for their skills in hunting and gathering, and later some were employed as watchmen and guards.
 
• Their traditional leadership and warrior skills were significant during the Maratha Empire.
 
 
 
• **British Policies and Impact**
 
 
• The British East India Company implemented policies that disrupted the traditional livelihoods of many tribal communities.
 
• Land revenue policies and forest laws restricted the Ramoshis' access to their traditional lands and resources.
 
• These policies led to widespread discontent and resistance among various tribal groups in India.
 
 
 
• **Other Tribal Uprisings**
 
 
• The Santal Rebellion (1855-56) in present-day Jharkhand and West Bengal.
 
• The Bhil Uprising (1818-1831) in western India.
 
• The Munda Rebellion (1899-1900) led by Birsa Munda in present-day Jharkhand.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**
 
 
• These uprisings were among the early signs of resistance against colonial rule in India.
 
• They reflect the widespread discontentment among various communities due to the exploitative policies of the British.
 
• Such uprisings set the stage for a broader national movement for independence in the later years.

questions.question: In 1927, B.R Ambedkar started which movement with Dalits?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temple entry movement.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Temple entry movement:-**

 
 
• **The Temple Entry Movement was a social movement in India that campaigned for the right of all Hindus, regardless of caste, to enter Hindu temples.**
 
• It was a major part of the Indian independence movement and played a crucial role in the fight against caste discrimination.
 
• **In 1927, B.R Ambedkar started this movement with Dalits.**
 
• The movement began in the early 20th century, when a number of social reformers began to challenge the practice of untouchability. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Respect Movement:-**

 
 
• **It was a social movement in South India that began in the early 20th century. **
 
• It was founded by E.V. Ramasamy
 
• It aimed to achieve a society in which oppressed castes have equal human rights, and encouraging backward castes to have self-respect in the context of a caste-based society that considered them to be a lower end of the hierarchy.
 
 
 
• **Equal Pay Movement:-**
 
 
• **It is a social movement that campaigns for equal pay for equal work, regardless of gender. **
 
• The movement has a long history, dating back to the early 19th century, but it gained momentum in the mid-20th century with the rise of the women's rights movement.
 
 
 
• **Indian independence movement:-**
 
 
• **It was a series of historic events with the ultimate aim of ending British rule in India.**
 
• It lasted from the mid-19th century to 1947, when India gained independence.

questions.question: Tirot Sing was the leader of which of the following revolts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khasi Uprising**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tirot Sing Syiem** was a chief of the Khasi people and is remembered for his pivotal role in resisting British colonial rule in the early 19th century.
 
• The **Khasi Uprising**, led by Tirot Sing, occurred in the year **1829** as a reaction to British incursions into Khasi territories for building a road connecting Assam and Sylhet.
 
• The revolt was triggered when Tirot Sing realized that the British were infringing upon Khasi sovereignty under the guise of constructing infrastructure.
 
• The Khasi tribes under Tirot Sing employed guerilla warfare to resist the British but were ultimately subdued due to superior British military tactics and resources.
 
• Tirot Sing was captured in **1833** and later died in captivity, symbolizing resistance against colonial oppression in Northeast India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khasi Hills:**

 
 
• The Khasi Hills are located in present-day Meghalaya, forming part of the Khasi-Jaintia Hills region.
 
• The Khasi people are one of the major indigenous ethnic groups in Northeast India, known for their matrilineal society.
 
 
 
• **Causes of the Khasi Uprising:**
 
 
• The British sought to construct a road through Khasi territory to connect **Guwahati (Assam)** with **Sylhet (now in Bangladesh)**.
 
• This was seen as an attempt to undermine the sovereignty of the Khasi chiefs.
 
 
 
• **Methods of Resistance:**
 
 
• The Khasis employed **guerrilla tactics**, using the hilly terrain to their advantage against British forces.
 
• The revolt was part of a broader pattern of localized tribal uprisings in India during the 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Tirot Sing:**
 
 
• Tirot Sing is a revered figure in Meghalaya, celebrated as a hero of resistance against colonial rule.
 
• His death anniversary is observed as a state holiday in Meghalaya, commemorating his fight for Khasi autonomy.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of 'Satnami movement' in the central India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ghasidas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ghasidas** was the founder of the **Satnami movement** in **central India**.
 
• The movement was initiated in the early **19th century** in the region that is now **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• It was a socio-religious reform movement that primarily aimed to uplift the **Dalit community** and combat caste-based discrimination.
 
• **Ghasidas** was a **spiritual leader** and preacher who emphasized the worship of **Satnam** (True Name), rejecting idol worship and promoting equality and simplicity.
 
• The Satnami movement emphasized the principles of **truth, equality, and spiritual purity** and was critical of the caste system prevalent in Hindu society.
 
• Ghasidas' teachings and the movement played a significant role in raising awareness about the **plight of marginalized communities** and encouraging social reforms.
 
• The movement continues to have a significant influence among the **Dalit and tribal communities** in Chhattisgarh and neighboring areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Narayan Guru**__

 __
 
• **Narayan Guru** was a **spiritual leader** and social reformer from **Kerala**, India.
 
• He advocated for **social equality**, rejecting caste-based discrimination in society.
 
• His teachings emphasized the importance of **education, social unity, and spiritual growth**.
 
• He established numerous **temples** that were open to all castes, challenging traditional norms.
 
 
 
• **Saint Haridas**__
 __
 
• **Saint Haridas** was a prominent figure in the **Bhakti movement**, known for his devotion to **Lord Krishna**.
 
• He was a **spiritual guru** of the famous Indian classical singer **Tansen**.
 
• His teachings primarily revolved around **devotional music** and worship.
 
• He is not associated with the **Satnami movement**.
 
 
 
• **Jyoti Rao Phule**__
 
 
• **Jyoti Rao Phule** was a prominent **social reformer** and activist from **Maharashtra**.
 
• He founded the **Satyashodhak Samaj**, focusing on the eradication of **caste discrimination** and promoting **education**, especially for women and marginalized communities.
 
• Although his work was revolutionary, he was not connected with the **Satnami movement**.

questions.question: Which newspaper was founded by Mahatma Gandhi in South Africa in 1903?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Indian Opinion.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Opinion **was started by **Mahatma Gandhi **in** South Africa.**
 
• This paper existed from **1903 to 1905** and served as a useful tool to fight against racial discrimination and thus played a key role in winning civil rights for the Indian immigrants in South Africa.
 
• The publication was an important tool for the political movement led by **Gandhi and the National Indian Congress** to fight racial discrimination and win civil rights for the Indian immigrant community in **South Africa.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Young India:**

 
 
• It was started by the** "Home Rule Party".**
 
• Young India was a weekly journal published under the supervision of **"Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi"** from the year **1919 to 1931.**
 
• This journal inspired many people as Gandhi write his quotations in it.
 
• This helped Gandhi in spreading his ideas and message to the people to motivate them in order to get freedom for Britain.
 
 
 
• **Hind Swaraj or Indian Home Rule:**
 
 
• It is a book written by** Mohandas K. Gandhi in 1909**.
 
• Expresses his views on Swaraj, modern civilization, mechanization, etc.
 
• The book was banned in **1910 **by the British government in India as a seditious text.
 
• Gandhi's Hind Swaraj takes the form of a dialogue between two characters,** "The Reader and The Editor".**

questions.question: ______ fought for the rights of the Dalit community.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Bhimrao Ambedkar.__** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** was an eminent lawyer, economist, and social reformer who fought for the cause of the Dalits for his whole life.
 
• He was born on **14 April 1891** in the small town of** Mhow** in the present M.P.
 
• He is regarded as the** "Father of the Indian Constitution" **as he served as the** Chairman of the Drafting Committee in the Constituent Assembly.**
 
• He also served as **the Minister of Law and Justice in the first Cabinet (1947-51) of Independent India.**
 
• He was also one of the parties of the famous **"Poona Pact" signed between Mahatma Gandhi and him in the year 1932.**
 
• He is also amongst the few persons who attended **all the three Round Table Conferences held in the year 1930,1931 and 1932 respectively.**
 
• He died on December 6, 1956, after **renouncing Hinduism and converting to Buddhism** along with his thousands of followers in **Nagpur.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The Moplah Uprising, an organised opposition of Muslim cultivators, occurred in which modern state of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Moplah Uprising, also known as the Mappila Rebellion, occurred in the Malabar region of Kerala in 1921.
 
• This rebellion was led by the Mappila Muslims of Kerala, who were primarily tenants and cultivators.
 
• The uprising was a reaction against British colonial rule and the oppressive practices of landlords.
 
• The rebellion saw widespread violence and was one of the significant peasant movements in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• It was part of the larger Khilafat Movement and Non-Cooperation Movement against British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khilafat Movement:**

 
 
• A pan-Islamist political campaign launched by Muslims in British India to influence the British government not to abolish the Ottoman Caliphate.
 
• It was led by prominent Muslim leaders like Maulana Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
 
 
 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement:**
 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, this was a mass protest against British rule.
 
• It aimed at inducing the British government to grant self-governance to India.
 
 
 
• **Malabar Region:**
 
 
• Located in the northern part of Kerala, the Malabar region was historically significant due to its trading ports.
 
• It was a major center for the spice trade and saw various foreign influences over centuries.
 
 
 
• **Tenant Farming:**
 
 
• A system where farmers cultivate land owned by another and pay rent in the form of cash or a portion of the produce.
 
• In the Malabar region, the oppressive practices by landlords led to widespread discontent among tenant farmers.

questions.question: The Oudh Kisan Sabha was set up in the year______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1920**__.

__
 
• **The Oudh Kisan Sabha was founded in 1920 by Baba Ram Chandra**__.

 __
 
• He was a trade unionist who gathered Oudh's farmers and led the first anti-landlord demonstration.
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra and others** founded the Oudh Kisan Sabha, commonly known as the Oudh Kisan Sabha.
 
• It was established to oppose the zamindars and talukdars who demanded excessive taxes and rent.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Some of the Movements:**

 
 
• Indigo Rebellion (1859-62)
 
• Pabna Movement (1870s-80s)
 
• Deccan Riots (1875)
 
• Champaran Satyagraha (1917)
 
• Kheda Satyagraha (1918)
 
• Moplah Rebellion (1921)
 
• Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)

questions.question: Who among the following led of the famous Indigo Revolt in Bengal?

options.text: Bishnu Charan Biswas and Digambar Biswas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ Bishnu Charan Biswas and Digambar Biswas__**.

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Indigo revolt

 
 
• The Indigo Revolt was a peasant movement and subsequent uprising of indigo farmers against indigo planters that erupted in **1859** in the Chaugacha village of Nadia, Bengal.
 
• The tenants were forced to grow indigo, which was processed in factories set up by indigo planters, almost all of whom were Europeans, in rural areas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Mahatma Gandhi

 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj in 1908 during his return visit to South Africa from India via London by ship.
 
• Hind Swaraj highlights all of Gandhi's basic principles, including the relationship between ends and means, between rights and duties, and between religious communities, as well as his concepts of history, nationality, dissent, education, and technology.
 
 
 
• Vasudeo Balwant Phadke : 
 
 
• He was born in the Raigad district of Maharashtra and belonged to the farming community and believed in Swaraj (Self-Rule).
 
• He got control of Pune in Maharashtra after catching British soldiers off-guard during a surprise attack. 
 
 
 
• ​Madari pasi
 
 
• Madari pasi led the Eka Movement along with many zamindars.
 
• The peasants assembled for Eka Movement meetings vowed that they would pay only the recorded rent.

questions.question: The All-India Kisan Sabha was founded in Lucknow in April _______ with Swami Sahjanand Saraswati as the president.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1936**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **All-India Kisan Sabha** (AIKS) was founded in **April 1936** at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The formation of AIKS was driven by the need to address issues concerning **land rights, rural exploitation, and agrarian reforms.**
 
• **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**, a prominent leader of farmers and peasants, was elected as the first president of the AIKS.
 
• The Sabha aimed to mobilize farmers, peasants, and agricultural workers for their **socio-economic and political rights**.
 
• It became closely associated with the **Indian National Congress** and played a significant role in the **freedom struggle**.
 
• The organization was instrumental in various **peasant movements**, particularly in regions like Bihar, Bengal, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• One of its key objectives was to abolish the **zamindari system** and secure fair land distribution for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Swami Sahajanand Saraswati**__

 __
 
• He was a prominent leader of the **peasant movement** in India and is often referred to as the **founder of the Kisan Sabha movement.**
 
• Sahajanand Saraswati authored several books, including **'Mera Jeevan Sangharsh' (My Life Struggle)**, which outlines his experiences and struggles for farmers' rights.
 
• He advocated for the abolition of the **zamindari system** and equal rights for peasants.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**__
 
 
• The **Indian National Congress (INC)** was the principal leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• The INC provided a platform for the formation of several organizations, including the **All-India Kisan Sabha**, to address specific societal and economic issues.
 
• Its session in **Lucknow (1936)** was significant as it highlighted the necessity of addressing rural and agrarian problems.
